title: Introduce RBAC quarantine workflow, KMS consent queue, and audit witness
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Context: Some operator-level actions (granting elevated operator roles, cross-region KMS wrap requests, and certain tenant-scoped key imports) require an additional approval/quarantine step for high-compliance customers. Motivation: Reduce blast radius from accidental or automated escalations, provide an auditable human consent trail for KMS operations, and give SRE/SEC teams an operator-friendly remediation path. Summary: This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) RBAC quarantine mode for operator grants: when a policy change matches configured quarantine predicates the decision is returned as 'quarantine' instead of allow/deny; the request is placed into a managed queue for review. 2) KMS consent queue: an internal queue that batches KMS grant/wrap requests requiring jurisdictional consent and records consent decisions as signed attestations. 3) Audit witness service: a lightweight append-only witness in the audit pipeline that links quarantined events, KMS queue entries, reviewer decisions, and evidence blobs. Changeset overview: - pkg/authorization/quarantine.go: new decision flow and predicate engine plus unit tests. - internal/kms/consent_queue/*: queue implementation, persistence adapter (sqlite-backed for local dev, Dynamo wrapper for prod), and metrics. - services/audit/witness/handler.go: witness recorder and integrity hash that is cross-referenced in tenant audit events. - api/handlers/operator_grants.go: integrates quarantine flow and surfaces queue IDs in API responses. - deploy/helm/redwood-operator/templates/quarantine-config.yaml: helm values to tune predicates, retention, and reviewer roster. - docs/security/quarantine-kms-consent.md: operator-facing runbook and migration guidance. Migration notes: This is opt-in per-tenant via a feature flag and helm values. Operators enabling this must provide KMS consent reviewers and set retention windows; rollout should be staged to a small set of tenants. Backwards compatibility: If the feature is disabled, decision behavior is unchanged. Checklist: - [x] predicate engine and unit tests - [x] end-to-end e2e test (k8s integration with sqlite persistence) - [x] metrics (queue length, time-to-approval, consent accept rate) - [x] audit witness cross-reference added to tenant audit log - [x] docs and runbook - [x] helm values and default disabled state Testing: Local unit tests and e2e suite executed. Initial CI run showed lint failures and one flaky e2e timing issue; fixes applied (formatting + extended timeout for sqlite-backed test). Security review: SEC review completed, notes addressed: non-repudiation of decisions via attestations, and KMS minimal-scope tokens used for queued operations. Observability: Added Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard snippets in observability-pack. Future work: UI for reviewers and paged queue, RBAC policy editor suggestions based on predicate telemetry, and optional automatic fallback after configurable SLA.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in RBAC quarantine workflow for operator-level grants, a KMS consent queue to manage jurisdictional KMS operations requiring human consent, and an audit witness to link decisions to audit logs. Disabled by default; operators must enable via helm values and configure reviewers.
manual_steps: Operators enabling this feature must: 1) add reviewer service accounts to the reviewer roster via helm values, 2) configure KMS reviewer keyring and short-lived consent signing key, 3) set retention and SLA thresholds in quarantine-config.yaml, 4) run migrator to create consent queue table in Dynamo (or enable sqlite for dev).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running queues could delay critical KMS operations. Mitigation: default SLA of 24h with automatic backoff alerting and optional force-approve CLI path requiring two approvers. Risk: accidental elevation loops—mitigation: predicate conservative defaults and opt-in per-tenant.
notes_for_release: Feature is disabled by default. Ops: if enabling in production, ensure reviewers are staffed and monitoring/alerts for queue depth and time-to-approval are configured. Consider a staged rollout: dev->canary->region->global.
